naming: The loader builds its YamlDotNet IDeserializer with CamelCaseNamingConvention + IgnoreUnmatchedProperties. A C# PascalCase property binds to the camelCase YAML key. The 'observances' enum is parsed case-insensitively.

keys.description: Selects the calendar document kind. Matched case-insensitively by YamlDocumentLoader.Parse.
The flow's unique identifier; seeds the stable FlowId. A blank value fails: "'name' is required for a calendar flow."
Free text carried on the flow and shown in the catalog.
Optional grouping label recorded with the run. Grouping/filter only; never an execution input and no effect on scheduling.

The flow's execution mode, read at the document envelope (YamlDocumentLoader's probe, FlowDocument.Mode) and projected to the catalog pipeline row. 'auto' (the default) runs on schedule fires and in batch/node group runs; 'manual' reserves a working flow for direct triggers; 'disabled' deactivates a retired one (a retired source, a run-once replay) with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. A node-scoped run can opt into includeAll ('find all') to replay non-auto descendants deliberately, and naming a flow directly always runs it.
keys.validation: Unknown value fails to load: "<source>: 'mode' has unknown value '<value>'. Allowed: auto, manual, disabled."

keys.description: A development flow runs identically but never generates notification events.
The document-local connection registry. Each value is either a plain string (a SQL Server connection reference) or a map with 'provider' and 'connection' keys.
The generator's declaration. Missing it fails with "'calendar' is required."

The connections alias the dimension is written to. Either this or a direct 'connection' is required. The target must be SQL Server (mssql/azdb); a foreign provider is rejected at parse time because the table is created and merged with T-SQL.
A direct connection literal instead of a named server; synthesized into the registry under the alias 'target'.
The provider of a direct 'connection'. Anything but mssql/azdb is rejected at parse time.

The three-part target table, Database.Schema.Table. The runner creates it (and its schema) when absent, with the generated column set plus InsertedDate_DW/UpdatedDate_DW and a clustered primary key on PeriodID.
First date in the dimension, inclusive. A value in any other form fails with "is not a date in yyyy-MM-dd form."

Last date in the dimension, inclusive. Must not precede 'from', and the span must not exceed 200 years (CalendarDimensionBuilder.MaxYears). The range never rolls forward on its own: widening it is a deliberate edit to the flow file.

Selects the observance rules and the season names, and supplies the default culture and time zone. Countries are added in code by implementing CountryCalendar; an unsupported value is a validation error naming the supported set.

The culture day and month names come from. Abbreviations are stored without their trailing period, so Norwegian emits 'man' and 'jan'. Resolved at parse time, so an unknown culture fails validate rather than a scheduled run.

The zone the DaylightSavingTime column and the astronomical observances resolve in. The legacy generator used the host's local zone, which made the result depend on which machine ran it. Resolved at parse time.

The month the fiscal year opens. FiscalYear is labelled by the calendar year the fiscal year STARTS in, so a January start makes FiscalYear equal the calendar year. FiscalWeekOfYear counts from 1 in the week containing the fiscal year's first day.

Which days are marked. 'full' is public holidays plus named days, eves, advent, equinoxes/solstices and the clock changes; 'publicHolidays' is the statutory days only; 'none' marks nothing. IsHoliday is NULL (never 0) on an unmarked day, because the reporting views branch on IS NULL.
Drop and recreate the target instead of merging into it. Off by default: the merge is idempotent, so a re-run refreshes in place and leaves any key downstream holds intact.

The document-envelope schedule, identical to every other flow kind. A calendar flow is normally MANUAL (the estate idiom: a named schedule with enabled: false and no cron), because a fixed range gives a recurring fire nothing to discover; the dimension changes when someone edits 'to:' and runs it by hand. A cron is still accepted and behaves as an assertion rather than an extension, reporting 0 inserted and 0 updated when nothing drifted.
